Estonia; standard foundation, informal examples marked

easy.meaning: Entry words and short everyday formulas

medium.meaning: Common vocabulary, longer requests and practical exchanges

hard.meaning: Informal register, contextual meanings and everyday native usage; not a CEFR level or proof of native proficiency

defaults_proposed_not_confirmed.interface_locale: Device locale when supported; otherwise en-US. Explicit user selection overrides device; this is a UI proposal, not supplied UI translations.
defaults_proposed_not_confirmed.lesson_access: All tiers browsable in this seed; progression not locked.
defaults_proposed_not_confirmed.suggestions: Deterministic topic/language suggestions; no live AI calls.
defaults_proposed_not_confirmed.guest_behavior: Bundle lessons, situations and translations locally; store progress/notes locally. Community/chat publishing needs network and an identity policy.

unresolved_product_questions.question: May the same language be both Know and Learn? Can selections change while retaining per-language progress?
unresolved_product_questions.blocks: Onboarding rules and progress migration, not seed import.

unresolved_product_questions.question: Who may approve/refuse content, and must situation authors approve proposed edits?
What defines mastery and exact review intervals?
unresolved_product_questions.blocks: Progress and awards, not content rendering.

unresolved_product_questions.question: Approve the proposed completion-with-help rule and non-punitive unmatched-answer behavior?
How should local guests become authenticated accounts, and how should local/server conflicts merge?
Does encryption mean transport/storage encryption or end-to-end encryption? Which attachment types and limits?
Does anonymous visibility mean read-only access without sign-in? Which content can guests see?
Confirm standard Indonesian/Estonian plus the labeled informal examples; should any particular city/region be targeted?

content_policy.production_publication_requires: Owner approval plus fluent/native review of target text, translations, context and answer alternatives.
content_policy.source_policy: Only linked headword/register facts were checked. Authored sentences and all multilingual equivalents are not independently native-reviewed. Source IDs do not certify an entire sentence or all translations.
content_policy.rights: No copied dictionary definitions, lesson passages, or dictionary example sentences. References are not licenses to scrape or redistribute a source database.
content_policy.private_data: No real user accounts, posts, chat messages, notes or learning progress are included.

grading_policies.accepted_match: Normalized exact match against authored accepted_answers.
grading_policies.unmatched: Not automatically semantically wrong. Offer retry/hint or self-review; mark progress as self-assessed if user accepts.

import_instructions: Validate schema version, locale set, unique IDs, all references and Unicode before importing.
Upsert global content by stable id and revision; do not duplicate records on app restart.
Bundle this JSON as a Flutter asset for guest/offline access; no runtime web requests are needed to read lessons.
Treat this as application seed JSON, not an existing Supabase table schema or direct SQL import. Map through repositories/migrations after schema decisions.
Keep source IDs, review states, variants and context attached when flattening records.
Use item.locale for the answer language. Filter item.translations to every selected Know language; use the selected prompt language for typing.
Do not grade a target-language word against its translated gloss. Never show the target answer in a typing prompt.
Shared concept_id groups one intended sense; never deduplicate entries by spelling alone. Native items deliberately have null concept_id.
On exposure or saving, create user-owned vocabulary/progress records separately; never modify the global seed or claim a word is mastered.
After a miss, increase local review priority; keep exact interval/mastery settings configurable pending decisions.
Use suggested discussions as composer starters, not fabricated activity from other people.
Queue user edits as drafts offline; do not auto-publish on reconnect without the confirmed posting/sync rules.
Keep unanswered architecture questions visible. Updated user answers supersede conflicting requirements in the earlier brief.

schema_notes.word_kind: Includes lexical units (e.g. horário marcado), not exclusively single orthographic tokens.
schema_notes.concept_id: Shared intended meaning for parallel foundational entries; null for locale-specific Native content.
schema_notes.source_ids: Supports headword sense/register only. Does not mean the source certified translations or difficulty.
schema_notes.publication_status: draft in every content entity; development preview allowed. Promote only through confirmed approval flow.
schema_notes.lesson_title_en: Editorial metadata only; localize navigation/lesson titles through the app UI localization layer.
schema_notes.full_know_translations: Every item and conversation turn includes all five other content locales; filter by Know languages at runtime.
schema_notes.schema_migration: An application seed document, not Supabase CSV import. Agent must adapt it to the confirmed schema.
schema_notes.segments: Every learning item has ordered segments. Concatenate segment.text without separators to reconstruct item.text byte-for-byte in UTF-8. Phrase boundary whitespace and punctuation are non-clickable segments with null IDs and empty translations.
schema_notes.segment_linguistic_units: Clickable phrase segments are manually aligned contextual words, inflected forms, or meaningful constructions. Fixed expressions, contractions, phrasal/compound predicates and discontinuous grammar may require a larger contiguous segment. Spaces/apostrophes/hyphens internal to such a unit remain inside it; boundary punctuation is separate. Word items intentionally use one whole-text clickable segment, including any original punctuation, as required by the uniform word rendering contract.
schema_notes.segment_translations: Every clickable segment contains all six locale keys, including its own locale. Translations express the contextual sense or grammatical function rather than a literal spelling lookup. They may use a natural phrase or an explanatory grammatical gloss when no independent equivalent exists; an unexpressed subject can be made explicit. No machine translation service is required at runtime. Existing needs_native_review status remains applicable to the new editorial mappings.
schema_notes.segment_meaning_ids: Existing concept IDs are reused for the same sense. New descriptive meaning IDs identify contextual senses/constructions and are independent of occurrence order or spelling. Identical spelling with a different sense must not share a meaning ID. IDs are stable through future wording edits that preserve the sense.
schema_notes.segment_lexical_item_ids: Optional exact-wording link to an existing same-locale, same-sense learning item. No case folding, punctuation stripping, substring matching or spelling-only sense guessing is used. Standalone word items self-reference. Null is expected for inflections and phrases without an exact standalone counterpart.
schema_notes.segment_validation: Required checks: nonempty arrays and nonempty texts; exact reconstruction; complete nonempty six-locale translations and meaning IDs for clickable units; null IDs/empty translations and no Unicode letters/numbers for non-clickable segments; existing exact-wording same-locale same-sense lexical targets; unique item IDs; valid lesson/exercise/Situation/source/community references; UTF-8 decode/round-trip; unchanged pre-existing item fields and all other content except schema_version, added schema notes and validation totals.
